title: Electrical Documentation Standards & Drawing Ownership
objective: Develop senior-level judgment for producing clear, consistent and reviewable electrical drawings from design intent through controlled issue.

learn.heading: What senior designers should understand
bullets: A drawing is a controlled technical deliverable, not merely a graphic representation of the design.
Distinguish design intent, drafting conventions, project standards and client-specific requirements before editing a drawing.
Use consistent sheet composition, tagging, notes, linework, symbols, references and revision information so a reviewer can interpret the design quickly.
Trace interfaces between electrical drawings and other disciplines rather than assuming missing information is harmless.
Perform a deliberate self-check before submitting work for checking: content, coordination, drafting quality, references, revision status and output.
senior_reasoning: How would you decide whether an inconsistency is a drafting issue, a design issue, or a project-standard issue?
What evidence would you gather before changing an established drawing convention?
How can a small documentation error create a larger construction, procurement or commissioning risk?

apply.scenario: You are asked to update a fictional electrical general arrangement and single-line drawing following several redline comments. Some comments are straightforward drafting corrections, while others require you to identify missing design information before making a change.
tasks: Classify each redline as drafting correction, design clarification, coordination issue or information gap.
Update the straightforward drafting items using consistent project conventions.
Create a clarification list for comments that should not be resolved by assumption.
Perform a self-check covering drawing content, tags, notes, references, revision information and plotted readability.
Write a short handover note explaining what was changed and what remains outstanding.
apply.deliverable: A sanitized redline response sheet or screenshot set plus a redline disposition table and self-check record.

questions.q: A redline says to relocate an electrical item, but the destination conflicts with a structural opening shown on a reference. What should you do first?
a: Move the item anyway because the redline is an instruction.
Check the coordination/design information and raise a clarification if the conflict cannot be resolved from approved information.
Move the item to any visually convenient location.
questions.why: Senior ownership means recognizing when a drafting action could change or conflict with design intent and resolving the information gap before proceeding.

questions.q: Which approach best demonstrates drawing ownership before issue?
a: Rely on the checker to find all problems.
Confirm technical content, coordination, drafting consistency, revision status and output quality against the applicable requirements.
Only inspect the areas mentioned in the latest redline.
Only confirm that the PDF was generated.
questions.why: A self-check should cover the complete deliverable, not only the last visible change.

questions.q: A note appears ambiguous but changing it would require inventing a technical value. What is the correct response?
a: Choose a reasonable value from memory.
Copy a value from an unrelated project.
Identify the information gap and seek the approved design input before finalizing the note.
questions.why: Drafting responsibility does not authorize inventing engineering information.

questions.q: Why should redline disposition be recorded?
a: To provide traceability of what was changed, clarified, deferred or rejected and support checking.
To replace the drawing revision process.
To avoid communicating with other disciplines.
questions.why: A clear disposition record supports traceability, review and controlled communication.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized redline disposition/self-check package demonstrating how you handled corrections, clarifications and coordination risks.
criteria: Assumptions are avoided where approved information is missing.
Changes and outstanding clarifications are traceable.
A complete self-check is documented before issue.

journal_prompt: Which redline or documentation decision required the most judgment, and what information did you use to decide whether to change the drawing or request clarification?
